title: Contextual history trimming notes
body:
Purpose: quick working notes for how we trim conversation history before labeling and how to surface edge cases for reviewers. Not a final guideline yet — this is where I scribble heuristics and examples to test on the 2k sample set.

Background: we frequently get long chat histories that push token limits. Trimming rules must preserve label-relevant context (entities, intents, previous confirmations) while removing noise (repeated chit-chat, long system banners, multi-turn small talk). Goal: maximize label fidelity with minimal context length.

High-level heuristics (working):
- Keep the most recent N user+assistant turns (configurable; start with last 6 turns).
- Always include the last user message in full.
- Preserve any system messages or directives that mention constraints, safety, or persona (if present anywhere in the convo).
- If a named entity is introduced earlier and later referenced (pronouns, ellipsis), keep the original turn that defines the entity + the last reference. Detection via simple regex for proper nouns + heuristics (capitalization + short tokens).
- Remove repetitive filler turns: repeated "lol"/"thanks" chains, single-token confirmations beyond the last 2 exchanges.
- If there is a timestamped code block or log snippet referenced later, keep the original snippet.

Edge cases to flag for manual review (examples below):
1) Disambiguation threads where the user asks clarifying Qs spread across early turns (e.g., "Do you mean X or Y?" earlier, final ask references X). Trimming might lose disambiguation context.
   - Example: earlier turn: "Do you mean local storage or cloud storage?" later: "Is it safe to store tokens in local storage?" If we drop the earlier turn we lose which meaning of 'storage' they considered.
   - Rule: if later turns contain pronouns with ambiguous antecedents, keep earlier clarifying turns.

2) Multi-party transcripts (user A and user B). If speaker labels exist, preserve the first mention of each speaker and the last exchange for each. If speakers are unlabeled, mark for human review.

3) Long quoted blocks (articles, messages pasted) that are later referenced: keep the title/first line + last 2 lines of the quote.

4) Bot-issued step-by-step instructions earlier in convo that user later asks to run: preserve the instruction anchor.

Trimming examples (Before -> After)
- Example A (simple):
  BEFORE:
  U1: "Hey, can you summarize the 1,200-word email I pasted earlier?"
  A: "Sure, paste it."
  U1: [long email] 
  A: "Summary..."
  AFTER (keep):
  - last user paste (long email) + assistant summary. Drop the earlier "Hey, can you..." opener if token savings needed.

- Example B (ambiguous pronoun):
  BEFORE:
  U: "We have two databases, users and sessions. Should we index it?"
  A: "Which one do you mean?"
  U: "The second one."
  A: "Ok, index sessions."
  LATER U: "Will that break analytics?"
  AFTER (must keep):
  - Keep the clarifying exchange that defines "the second one" -> otherwise "that" is ambiguous.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Threshold for 'recent N turns' — run experiments with N=4,6,8 on 2,000 convo sample, compare label agreement drop. (JIRA:LAB-2147 assigned but need more stats)
- Should we rely on simple heuristics for entity coreference or run a lightweight coref model? Tradeoff: cost vs fewer manual reviews.
- Edge-case detector: produce a binary "needs-review" flag when (a) multiple speakers, (b) ambiguous pronouns, (c) important entities appear > X tokens before last turn. Tune X.
- Add a quick UI preview showing what was dropped so reviewer can rehydrate context if they think trimming hurt label quality.

Quick manual reviewer checklist (for flagged rows):
- Does the trimmed context still let you unambiguously answer the label question? y/n
- Are there unresolved pronouns or references? If yes, rehydrate earlier turns until references resolved.
- Is there critical system or safety instruction missing? If yes, re-add.

Sample rows to pull for testing (query to QA):
- Long customer support threads where policy/privilege was mentioned early and later referenced.
- Chat transcripts with code blocks and stack traces.
- Threads with interleaved small talk that can be compressed.

Notes to self: when I run sampling, export examples with both versions (full vs trimmed) and put side-by-side in review sheet (sheet id in linked_artifacts). Track labeler disagreement and "needs rehydrate" counts.

Slack threads I referenced: #data-labeling (thread ts: 1703214123.000200) - there was a convo about keeping system instructions; collect messages into the confluence page.

Final-ish thought: we should aim for deterministic, explainable trimming steps so reviewers can predict what gets removed. Anything ML-driven should produce an explanation ("removed because repetitive filler detected: 6 tokens repeated").

-- end scratchpad --
